# Building with the plan stage off

`accord anchor` printed `stages off for lane <L>:` naming plan. There is no `plan.md`: the whole ticket is one task,
task 1.

Before step 1, when `tests.report` is set and `accord/tests-baseline.txt` is absent, take the tests baseline, before any
executor is dispatched, as `./plan-baseline.md` says: nothing else asks for it with the plan stage off, and
without it every test case already in the suite counts as untraced. Run `tests.full` only while `git status --porcelain`
(staged, unstaged and untracked paths) lists no path outside `accord/` and `git diff --stat <fork point>` (the fork
point is `git merge-base HEAD <default branch>`; it covers commits and the working tree) shows none either; otherwise ask
the owner. An
executor leaves its work uncommitted until step 4, so a resumed run on a dirty tree has an executor's code in it. Never
take the baseline after an executor has written code. There is no plan-ready commit: the baseline commit stays alone, and
its Ruling goes into the ledger commit of step 4.

1. Run `accord brief <id> 1 --out brief-1.md`, which writes the brief into the git-ignored `.accord-reports/<id>/` folder, so it is
   never committed, and dispatch one fresh `accord-executor` with the path its `file:` line prints, only. Never pass chat history.
   The brief holds the whole ticket.

2. When it reports, run the test command the brief printed yourself: `tests.affected`, or `tests.full` when the brief
   says no `tests.affected` is set. When it printed neither, run the test files the executor reports it wrote or changed.

3. Read from the executor's report which test proves each scenario that is not `@ui`. Run `accord task-done <id> 1
   --test ac-<n>=<test id>` once, with one `--test` pair for every such scenario; a `@ui` scenario takes no pair.
   The executor's claim alone records nothing.

4. When it refuses, handle it as step 3 of `./build.md` handles a refusal of `accord task-done <id> <n>`: a failed or
   absent test, or a scenario with no pair, gets a fresh executor with the same brief plus the reasons it printed, and
   a second refusal of that kind loads `accord-debug`; a missing or old `tests.report` file, an executor report that is
   missing, old or lacks its lines, a forbidden commit line, or a scenario that already carries a different `@test:` tag
   are handled as it says. On success it writes the ledger
   line and the `@test:` tags: copy every Ruling in the executor's report into `accord/tickets/<id>/ledger.md` under
   `## Rulings`, commit the ticket with the ledger, then run `accord worktree push <id>`; go on even if it fails.

5. With the plan stage off there is no plan stage (`./plan.md`) to go back to: a block that steps 4 and 7 of `./build.md` send
   there goes to the owner, and after a change of course (step 6) the new yes is followed by `accord brief <id> 1`
   again.

6. Next: `./review.md`. When `accord anchor` names review off, follow the section `With the review stage off` of `./review-security.md`, then `./verify.md`.
